perspective:
From Gloria Bangura’s perspective:

- I noticed Donald seemed less enthusiastic and somewhat distracted while serving drinks during company events. This wasn’t just one time—I observed it over several events.
- I approached him and asked if he was okay with the job. He told me, “I guess I’m just not as into it as I used to be. It’s kind of repetitive.”
- After thinking it over, I suspected his work dissatisfaction might be connected to something deeper. I suggested he consider talking to a professional. He replied, “I haven’t really considered that... I’m not sure if that would help.”
- After that conversation, I sensed a shift in his behavior toward me and worried he might have felt I overstepped. I apologized and told him I only wanted to help. He said he was “a bit taken aback at first” but knew I meant well and that it was “a lot to process.”
- Relieved that we cleared the air, I invited him to collaborate on a new project. He accepted, saying he appreciated it and wanted to be more involved.
- During the project, I observed his strong contributions and renewed enthusiasm. In a team meeting, I publicly acknowledged his work, saying his efforts were crucial. He thanked me and said it felt great to be appreciated.
